title: Medical AI in the Waiting Room: A Survey of Foundation Models and Agent Systems Toward Clinical Readiness
content: Medical AI has advanced from task-specific models toward foundation models and agent systems that organize heterogeneous clinical evidence, conduct multi-step reasoning, and execute actionable workflows. We argue that clinical readiness requires simultaneously satisfying four principles—evidence sufficiency, reasoning trustworthiness, decision controllability and auditability, and specialty adequacy. These principles reveal two fundamental tensions: model vs. system and generalist vs. specialist, whose intersection yields four research paradigms. Using these principles as analytical anchors, we examine each paradigm's contributions and capability boundaries. We identify four persistent gaps separating current research from clinical readiness: insufficient evidence-sufficiency guarantees, unresolved reasoning trustworthiness, system-level governance deficits, and tension between specialty depth and generalization. We conclude that medical AI maturity depends not on peak task performance but on sustaining equilibrium among these principles.
